subject: elephant
pitch: A gentle African elephant calf. Wrinkly slate-grey skin with a dusty, reddish tint from rolling in the dirt, huge fan-shaped ears with a pink flush on the inside, a curious trunk curling forward, stubby baby tusks, long lashes over kind brown eyes, a little tufted tail and round, padded feet with pale toenails.
reasoning:
I'm planning the elephant calf's structure: a modest shoulder height around 1 meter, facing forward, with a skeleton built from hips through a spine chain to the neck and head, plus legs, trunk, ears, jaw, and tail.

Working out joint placements for hips, spine, neck, head, and jaw, chaining parents and positions along the body, then sizing the head as a scaled sphere near the top of the neck.

Now I'm defining the body sweep path along the spine, deciding which bone chains drive the cross-section, and setting up the elliptical radius profile with a mottled reFor the body shape, I'm sweeping a catmull path from rear to front using the spine bones with an elliptical cross-section, and planning a mottled coat paint that shifts toward dustier tones near the feet using noise, mix, and smoothstep functions.

For the texture layering, I'm nesting gradient and stripes paints to build wrinkle bands over the mottled base, picking a vertical axis for the creases so legs and trunk both read as horizontally banded skin, and skipping countershading for now.

Now I'm setting up leg joint positions, placing hips and feet coordinates symmetrically on each side using a side multiplier for left/right offset.

Working out leg geometry... straight-legged chains with shoulder, knee, ankle points, tapered radius function, and a cylindrical foot pad to close off the sweep at the bottom.

Now I'm adding toenails as small pale boxes fanned around the front of each foot cylinder, positioning them by angle and attaching them to the ankle bone's tip joint, then mirroring the setup for the hind legs with their own hip/knee/ankle positions.

I'm also mapping out the skeleton hierarchy -- hind legs parenting to the hips and front legs parenting to the second spine joint -- while refining the body shape with rounded caps and radii along the z-axis path to get the proportions right.

Now I'm placing the head sphere forward and slightly elevated, adding a forehead bump and cheeks, then connecting a short neck sweep between the body and head to complete the rig.

For the trunk, I'm plotting curling catmull points that drop down from the head front before tipping forward and up at the tip, mimicking a natural downward-then-curl trunk shape.

Placing dark nostril spheres near the trunk tip, offset slightly from the rounded end to sit naturally on the surface.

Now I'm adding a mouth and jaw: a small pink-grey box positioned beneath the trunk base to form the lower jaw bone.

For tusks, I'm placing stubby ivory spikes beside the trunk base using the spike helper, angled outward and downward with a short length and small radius, attached to the head bone.

Now I'm positioning the eyes as dark brown spheres embedded slightly into the head surface, calculating placement so they sit within the head radius, with small white highlight spheres and a ring of lash spikes around each eye.

Next I'll shift to the ears, which need a large fan-shaped outline extruded in the ear's plane.

Still defining ear outline points...

Defining ear coloring logic...

Now I'm working out the ear geometry and attachment: setting thickness, bevel, and placement near the head with a hinge joint, then sizing the ear span appropriately since calf ears tend to be fairly large.

Next I'm building the tail as a short bone chain from the rump down through two or three joints, sweeping its radius thinner toward the tip, and adding a tuft of spike clusters at the end using a ring of spikes in a dark coat color.

For the crown fuzz, I'll filter hits to the upper region and place small dark cone spikes deterministically using a seeded scatter. I'll skip knee wrinkles, cheeks, and temples, keeping the stripes as the main texture, but consider dust patches gradating across the back.

Now I'm layering coat textures: mottled slate skin combined with axial wrinkle stripes, then applying a dust gradient down the legs for a weathered look, using a rust-brown dust color. I'll paint body parts and the foot cylinder with this same coat material so the coloring stays continuous across the model, then move on to sculpting the belly using a bone-driven sweep path along the spine chain.

I'm working out the spine path points and reconsidering whether to anchor the sweep to the hips or spine bone, since the chain's rounded caps risk stretching the body too long -- the rump cap pushing back past -0.6 and the chest cap extending too far forward would make the torso over a meter long, so I need to rethink the path length and cap radii.

Placing the trunk path from the head forward face, curving down and forward then up slightly at the tip, while checking the head sphere's position and radius align with where the trunk should attach.

I'm now positioning the tusks and jaw joint relative to the trunk base, sizing the jaw box and checking it doesn't clip with the trunk, then placing eye spheres on the head surface and verifying their offset falls just within the head radius so they poke out naturally.

I'm also figuring out ear placement and orientation vectors, adding a forehead bump sphere scaled to sit above the head's back curve, and setting up a left/right mirroring convention based on sign. For the legs, I'm wiring up the toenail and foot joints through the bone chain's tip, parenting front legs to the spine and hind legs to the hips, then sweeping tapered leg geometry along each chain with flat end caps so the feet terminate cleanly.

Now I'm sorting out imports needed from the builder library and deciding to pass raw point arrays into chain and sweep calls rather than smoothing them, since the limb joints should stay sharp at corners like knees. I'm also adding a tuft of spike hairs around the tail tip using a ring generator, and placing nostril spheres at the end of the trunk's joint chain before writing out the final code.
